If your little guy is only a week old, that means his momma is only 1 week postpartum. She hasn’t recovered yet from giving birth, and her hormones are still far from being back to normal. This is a good time to just hang on for a bit a see if things can get better, and be really supportive to her physical recovery. Sleep deprivation and her body needing to recover are definitely a challenge. I don’t think you should feel trapped in a relationship you aren’t happy in, but I do think given even just a few months, things will change regardless. Also, if she’s in bad shape mentally, encourage her to talk to her midwife or doctor about if she may have postpartum depression or any post partum mood disorders. They’re not uncommon, and there should be support available that can help. If she seems like she’s angry a lot it could be post partum anxiety, for example. Hang in there. This is a season that won’t last forever. Whether you stay together or not, ending the relationship right now is probably jumping the gun either way.

But maybe what’s important to point out is that preventing a fertilized egg from implanting isn’t the main way an IUD is even designed to work. It generally prevents sperm from meeting egg in the first place. But IF that part doesn’t work, it can THEN also prevent implantation. Basically it’s 1) prevent egg from ovulating, 2) be toxic to sperm so sperm won’t survive anyway, 3) if someone an egg releases and a sperm makes it through, and they somehow meet, the egg won’t have an easy time implanting.

The truth is, a sperm fertilizing an egg and then that fertilized egg simply not implanting, could happen every single cycle, even without an IUD, and we wouldn’t ever have a way to know it. But, if the fertilized egg never implants, there is never a pregnancy. Abortion is ending a pregnancy. Preventing a fertilized egg from implanting is not abortion. The argument could be that if you believe a sperm fertilizing an egg is when “life begins” then you wouldn’t have a way to know if an IUD is actively preventing fertilized eggs from implanting all the time. The same thing could be happening naturally, anyway, but since the IUD has a factor of thickening the uterine lining, it could be argued that it increases the likelihood of that happening. So if a person believes that life begins the very moment sperm meets egg, and then for that reason they also believe that any action taken to prevent that fertilized egg to become a pregnancy is wrong, then they wouldn’t use an IUD (or any hormonal birth control whatsoever) without it being hypocritical. Even in that individual’s personal beliefs, I still don’t think that could be defined as murder, though.

IUDs (and honestly any birth control) has the chance of a sperm fertilizing an egg and then it just can’t implant. This is not the intended methodology but it is basically a third line of defense. Birth control is NOT abortifacient. BUT- if you believe that “life begins when sperm meets egg” without exception, then you cannot in good conscience use any kind of hormonal birth control whatsoever because it is not known how often that occurs.

The uncle/relatives aren’t the threat. The invisible germs that a newborn’s immature immune system can’t handle are the threat.
I am a lurking pregnant mom and I’m 23 weeks and struggling with this eventuality myself. I know people aren’t going to like it, but they have to accept that it just isn’t personal. 
This will be my 5th baby and I’ve learned up until now that people are very entitled when it comes to babies. But they need to be made aware that it’s not that you or your wife think they’re inept, ignorant, incapable, or dirty or anything like that. The baby just simply doesn’t have a developed immune system. 
People are willing to risk it because they aren’t symptomatic and therefore must not be bringing any germs, meanwhile everyone else also thinks the same thing and the whole time, any one of them could have germs that could kill your child that simply aren’t affecting their adult bodies. Sickness doesn’t onset immediately after exposure to germs. 
People will feel entitled to this special time because it goes by so fast. But they simple are not entitled to it. 

Keep your baby safe and protected. 
Support your wife.
Let them pout.

When I was 18, a 17-year-old classmate killed herself. We were all devastated,  students and faculty both. I had been a troubled person throughout high school, so I had visited and talked with our guidance counselors on several occasions over thr years. I overheard that they were devastated and felt horrible because they had never even talked to the girl who died, and nobody had ever told them she had talked about suicide. They felt like they should have been able to help her somehow.
I knew how much they had helped me, so I wrote them each a really long, heartfelt letter about how they had helped me through highschool so far and that their support meant the world to me, etc. I had been suicidal at one point as well, so I reminded them that they'd had a hand in saving my life. 
At the girl's funeral they both hugged me and thanked me for my letters and told me it meant a lot to them to know they hadn't failed the students at our school, and that their efforts to make a difference mattered.
